note: The Lean Canvas (Maurya, Running Lean, 2012; adapted from Osterwalder's Business Model Canvas) as the venture's shared kernel (Evans, Domain-Driven Design): one page every function reads. Each box is a reference to a record attribute its owning function writes, never a copy, so a box cannot drift from its record. The strategy function owns the canvas itself, which only assembles and orders the boxes. packages/naive/src/engine/lean-canvas.ts resolves it for a venture (EE-155).

standard.name: Lean Canvas
standard.source: Ash Maurya, Running Lean: Iterate from Plan A to a Plan That Works, O'Reilly, 2012
standard.adapted_from: Alexander Osterwalder and Yves Pigneur, Business Model Generation, Wiley, 2010

boxes.label: Problem
boxes.ask: What are the top problems your customers have, and how do they solve them today?

boxes.label: Customer segments
boxes.ask: Who has the problem, and who are the early adopters?

boxes.label: Unique value proposition
boxes.ask: What single, clear message says why you are different and worth buying?

boxes.label: Solution
boxes.ask: What is the smallest thing that solves each problem?

boxes.label: Channels
boxes.ask: How do you reach your customers?

boxes.label: Revenue streams
boxes.ask: How do you make money, and at what price?

boxes.label: Cost structure
boxes.ask: What does it cost to acquire customers, build and run the product?

boxes.label: Key metrics
boxes.ask: Which numbers tell you the venture is working?

boxes.label: Unfair advantage
boxes.ask: What do you have that cannot be easily copied or bought?
